department: Department of Biomedical Engineering (CU Denver CEDC / CU Anschutz)

deadline.value: Apply by December 1, 2026 for Fall admission (no Spring admission).
deadline.quote: Please note that the PhD application window closes on December 1 for all applicants.

also.quote: Biomedical Engineering Master of Science (MS) Fall: July 15 Spring: November 20 Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) Fall: December 1 Spring: No spring admission

gre_general.value: GRE scores are optional and not considered in admission decisions.
gre_general.quote: GRE scores are not considered in admission decisions.

also.quote: GRE scores are not required. If choosing to submit, send scores officially through ETS using code #4875.

gre_subject.value: ETS offers no GRE Subject Test in Biomedical Engineering, and GRE scores are not considered.
gre_subject.quote: GRE scores are not considered in admission decisions.

also.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Pre-application supervisor requirement for external PhD applicants is not stated on admissions pages; the department handbook notes some students may be admitted to complete lab rotations while continuing MS-to-PhD students identify a funded mentor.

also.quote: At the discretion of the department and the admissions committee, some students may be admitted with the expectation that they rotate through laboratories for one or two semesters in order to choose a lab.

funding.value: All new Bioengineering PhD students receive an annual stipend, health insurance coverage, and full tuition at admission (continued funding depends on mentor funding, grants, and satisfactory progress; note CEDC's general graduate admissions page carries a caveat that financial support is not guaranteed across all engineering programs).
funding.quote: All new PhD students are offered a stipend plus tuition, fees, and health insurance at the time of admission.

also.quote: PhD graduate students admitted to the Bioengineering program receive an annual stipend, health insurance coverage and full tuition.

entry_route.value: Apply with a bachelor's degree in engineering, physical sciences, or a bioscience-related field (with calculus, differential equations/linear algebra, and physics; 3.0 GPA preferred).
entry_route.quote: Applicants to the PhD or Master of Science in Biomedical Engineering should meet the following minimum requirements: Completion of a bachelor's degree in engineering or physical sciences from an accredited United States institution or comparable international institution, or Completion of a bachelor's degree in a bioscience-related field with the following courses: Calculus I, II, and Differential Equations/Linear Algebra

notes: Dual-campus CU Denver College of Engineering, Design and Computing and CU Anschutz Medical Campus Biomedical Engineering PhD (60 credits: 30 coursework + 30 dissertation). Diplomas list both CU Denver and CU Anschutz.
